record.paper_title: A review of four decades of time-dependent scheduling: main results, new topics, and open problems
record.context_brief: Linear deterioration with precedence and makespan
record.original_question: Given n jobs to be scheduled on a single machine with arbitrary precedence constraints represented by an acyclic directed graph, where job j has linearly deteriorating processing time p_j(t) = a_j + b_j t when it starts at time t, determine the computational complexity of minimizing the makespan C_max = max_j C_j. Is this precedence-constrained linearly deteriorating scheduling problem NP-hard at least in the ordinary sense, or is it polynomial-time solvable?

evidence.quote: 1|p j=a j+b j t, prec|C max

artifact.self_contained_problem: Consider the following single-machine scheduling problem. A set of n jobs J_1, ..., J_n must be processed without preemption on a single machine that is continuously available from time t = 0. Each job J_j has linearly deteriorating processing time: if J_j starts at time t ≥ 0, then its processing time is p_j(t) = a_j + b_j t, where a_j ≥ 0 and b_j ≥ 0 are given rational constants. Precedence constraints between the jobs are given by an arbitrary acyclic directed graph G on the vertex set {J_1, ..., J_n}; if there is an arc from J_i to J_j then J_i must be completed before J_j can start. Let C_j denote the completion time of job J_j in a feasible schedule, and let C_max = max_{1 ≤ j ≤ n} C_j be the makespan. The task is to determine the computational complexity of finding a feasible schedule that minimizes C_max. Specifically: is this problem NP-hard (at least in the ordinary sense), or does there exist a polynomial-time algorithm that solves it?
artifact.status_search_result: Searches in the time-dependent scheduling literature (including Gawiejnowicz's monograph and follow-up surveys) list the single-machine problem with general linear deterioration p_j = a_j + b_j t and arbitrary precedence constraints minimizing C_max among problems whose complexity status is not definitively settled; results are known only for special structures (chains, equal a_j or b_j, proportional deterioration). No source verifying a polynomial algorithm or an NP-hardness proof for the fully general precedence case was found.

status_evidence.claim: The general precedence-constrained single-machine problem with linear deterioration is listed among problems whose complexity has not been fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: Scheduling jobs with chain precedence constraints and deteriorating jobs
status_evidence.snippet: Considers chain precedence constraints with deteriorating jobs, providing results for restricted precedence structures.
status_evidence.claim: Polynomial/known-complexity results exist only for restricted precedence structures such as chains, not for arbitrary acyclic precedence graphs.
